sections.overview: Lethrinus ravus Carpenter & Randall, 2003 is a marine emperor fish in the family Lethrinidae.
sections.identification: A relatively small emperor, it reaches about 25 centimetres standard length and has a pale grey or tan body with scattered dark blotches.
sections.habitat: It occurs from the western Pacific to the eastern Indian Ocean, on or near reefs at roughly 5–35 metres depth.
sections.diet: The consulted species accounts do not provide a well-supported, detailed diet description.
sections.behavior: It is observed alone or in small groups near reefs.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted provide little species-specific information on reproduction.
sections.ecology: The original description identifies L. semicinctus as its closest look-alike and probable sister species; the companion profiles of L. obsoletus and L. reticulatus add two other Lethrinus for comparison.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment dated 2015 classified it as Least Concern.
